children: Harsha Gopal Kadam was taken into custody after a June gas leak killed two contract workers at the company's Talegaon plant; Schaeffler says operations remain unaffected

Schaeffler India Managing Director and CEO Harsha Gopal Kadam was taken into police custody on 19 October in connection with a factory accident in Pune that killed two workers in June. The company disclosed the development in a regulatory filing on 20 October, as the investigation widened to include its top executive.

The development brings the head of the Indian subsidiary of German auto components maker Schaeffler into the investigation into the 9 June incident at its Talegaon facility. The company said Kadam was taken into custody by the Talegaon MIDC Police Station under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, on the grounds that he is considered the occupier of the factory premises under applicable law.
Schaeffler India said its senior management continues to oversee daily operations and that business activities remain unaffected.

The accident occurred on 9 June 2026, at Schaeffler India's Talegaon factory in Pune district, when carbon dioxide gas was suddenly discharged during a scheduled cylinder replacement. The two workers who died were employed by a service provider to the company, according to its regulatory disclosure.

Police had reportedly registered a case in July against six people, including company officials and representatives of contractors involved in maintaining the fire-suppression system. A report by The Indian Express, said the first information report raised questions about ventilation, emergency exits, trained personnel and rescue arrangements at the site. These are allegations under investigation and do not establish criminal liability.
Company Says Operations Continue As Usual

Schaeffler India said it and its officers had cooperated with the investigation and would continue to do so. The company is evaluating the developments in consultation with its legal advisers and said it would take the necessary steps in accordance with applicable law.

The company also said it had complied, and continued to comply, with applicable laws. Its regulatory filing stated that senior management remained in charge of day-to-day administration and that business operations continued in the ordinary course following Kadam's detention.
